cards.explanation: The answer is the grace coming when Jesus Christ is revealed. Peter says to "Set your hope fully on the grace to be given you at the revelation of Jesus Christ." Notice the word fully, friends. He doesn't say save a little hope for the oven and a little for the bank account. All of it goes in one place.

The answer is False. Peter says, "As obedient children, do not conform to the passions of your former ignorance." So he's telling them not to let those old passions press their shape onto them anymore. Don't be the cookie that goes back into the old mold, friends.

The answer is because the One who called them is holy. Peter says, "…just as He who called you is holy, so be holy in all you do…" and then points to Scripture: "Be holy, because I am holy." The reason isn't a rule list, friends. It's who called them. When the One who calls you is holy, that's the whole reason.

The answer is in reverent fear. Peter says, "Since you call on a Father who judges each one’s work impartially, conduct yourselves in reverent fear…" Reverent means they take Him seriously and honor Him. It's the kind of respect where you stand up straighter when the Father walks in the room.

The answer is foreigners. Peter says to conduct themselves in reverent fear "…during your stay as foreigners." That fits how he opens the letter, writing to God's chosen people scattered across places like Pontus and Galatia (1 Peter 1:1). A foreigner knows this isn't home, friends, and I know a little about being far from the kitchen.

The answer is True. Peter says, "…it was not with perishable things such as silver or gold that you were redeemed…" Silver and gold are the things you'd expect to pay with, friends. Peter says that's not what bought them back, and he tells us what did in the next verse.

The answer is the precious blood of Christ. Peter says they were redeemed "…with the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish or spot." Precious is Peter's word for it, and it fits. Not silver, not gold, but the blood of Christ.

The answer is in the last times for their sake. Peter says Christ "…was known before the foundation of the world, but was revealed in the last times for your sake." Your sake means the very people Peter is writing to. I think that's worth a pause, friends, because it's personal.

The answer is hope. Peter writes, "…your faith and hope are in God." He says it right after telling them God raised Christ from the dead and glorified Him. So their faith and hope rest on the God who did that, friends.

The answer is to love one another deeply from a pure heart. Peter says, "…love one another deeply, from a pure heart." They've purified their souls by obedience to the truth so they'd have genuine love, and now he tells them to use it. Love like that has to get out of the box and onto the counter, friends.

The answer is the living and enduring word of God. Peter says they've been born again "…through the living and enduring word of God." (1 Peter 1:23) Living and enduring, both at once, friends. Peter even sets it against "perishable seed," and says this seed is imperishable (1 Peter 1:23).

The answer is False. The Scripture says, "All flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flowers of the field; the grass withers and the flowers fall…" They fade and drop. I'm glad the verse puts the glory part in there, friends, because I was a little worried about my mustache.

The answer is that it stands forever. The Scripture says, "…the word of the Lord stands forever." Grass withers, flowers fall, and the word is still standing. It's the one thing in the whole picture that doesn't fade, friends.
